heading: INT. FUNICULAR CAR, HALFWAY UP - NIGHT

units.text: INT. FUNICULAR CAR, HALFWAY UP - NIGHT
A wood-paneled funicular car stalled on a steep incline above a sleeping Swiss lake town.
Rain on the glass.
One brass lamp burns.
MADAME ODILE VANTERPOOL (60s, fur collar, rings on every finger) sits very upright on the forward bench.
Across from her, INSPECTOR HOLLIS CRANE (40s, rumpled trench coat, a hat he keeps turning in his hands) studies the floor.
Neither speaks.
Wind shifts the car.
The cable creaks.
An intercom grille crackles beside the door.
Folks, we have a fault on the lower winch. Twenty minutes, perhaps thirty. Please remain seated.
units.name: OPERATOR

units.text: Crane glances at the grille, then at Odile, who has not looked up.
She opens her handbag, takes out a small pearl-handled revolver, sets it on her knee as one might set down a glove, and closes the bag again.
Crane watches this, sets his hat on the bench beside him, and slides a hand slowly into his coat pocket and out again with a cigarette case.
He offers her one.
She declines with two fingers.
He lights his own, and the match shakes just once.
Terrible weather.
units.name: CRANE

units.text: It does this in October.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: Your husband used to say that, I understand.
units.name: CRANE

units.text: My husband said a great many things.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: The lamp flickers.
Crane exhales smoke toward the ceiling.
He was found at the bottom of this very hill. Same hour. Same rain.
units.name: CRANE

units.text: I heard.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: You didn't come to the funeral.
units.name: CRANE

units.text: I was unwell.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: Yet here you are, riding the last car of the night, to a villa you've told everyone you have not visited in a year.
units.name: CRANE

units.text: She turns the revolver a quarter-inch on her knee, so the muzzle points at the door instead of at him.
Inspector, you've been very patient. Say what you came to say.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: The conductor remembers a woman in a fur collar on the evening car. The night of.
units.name: CRANE

units.text: The conductor is mistaken.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: He was very sure. He said she tipped him. Said she wore rings on every finger.
units.name: CRANE

units.text: Silence.
The cable creaks.
Odile lays one ringed hand flat over the revolver and does not lift it.
Fault located. Ten more minutes, folks. Thank you for your patience.
units.name: OPERATOR

units.text: Crane stubs the cigarette out on the sole of his shoe and puts the butt in his pocket, neat as ever.
Odile picks up the revolver and holds it in her lap with both hands.
Crane does not reach for his hat.
He does not reach for anything.
You could shoot me. Before they get the car moving.
units.name: CRANE

units.text: I could.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: Nobody would hear it over the rain.
units.name: CRANE

units.text: No.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: Then why haven't you?
units.name: CRANE

units.text: She stands.
The car sways.
The muzzle comes up, level, steady, and she crosses the three steps between them and puts it against his tie.
Because you are the first person in a year who has said his name aloud to me.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: She pulls the hammer back.
Odile.
units.name: CRANE

units.text: The intercom crackles.
The car lurches forward and begins to climb.
And we're moving! Sorry for the delay!
units.name: OPERATOR

units.text: The lamp swings.
Her finger tightens.
